title: Moonscape Retail pilot outreach notebook
content:
Topline: quick raw notebook for Moonscape (omnichannel retail merchandising + personalization). Goal is a 6–8 week pilot to validate: latency impact of real-time personalization, inference cost per 10k user sessions, and ease of integrating Redwood Dedicated or Private into their infra.

Quick context / why them:
- Moonscape is a mid-market omnichannel retail platform (250 stores + web/mobile). Heavy personalization stack already but slow A/B tests and expensive infra for newer transformer-based rerankers.
- Public signals: posted about latency issues in their engineering blog (Sept ’24), hiring ML infra lead in SF. That reads as a timing + budget window.
- Likely concerns: data residency for EU customers, rollout risk for store-critical systems, and headcount to maintain an on-prem solution.

Primary hypotheses we can test in pilot:
1) Replace their current reranker (bi-encoder + logistic) for web search with a Redwood-hosted rerank model variant and measure uplift in CTR and conversion within 6 weeks.
2) Demonstrate ~30–50% lower per-token cost using caching + batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize vs their naive inference.
3) Show safe fallback: when Dedicated capacity saturated, our routing to a quantized model keeps storefronts online with <5% degraded conversions.

Key contacts (scraped / notes):
- Product: Lena Ortiz (Head of Product, personalization) — LinkedIn active, previously at AcmeRetail.
- ML infra: Marco De la Cruz (hired Oct ’24) — likely primary technical champion.
- Platform / IT: Ravi Menon (VP Platform) — security and compliance gate.
- Buyer (revenue): Priya Shah (Director Growth) — cares about conversion lift and CAC.

Why Redwood message should resonate:
- We can run the same model variants across hosted + private (for stores) so they don’t have to hire a new infra team for model ops.
- Cost levers (Optimize) are concrete: caching, batching, quantization recommendations + predicted $/session.
- Rollouts & fallback: built-in canary + automatic fallback to smaller variants during peak traffic. They’ve called this out as a current pain.

POC idea (minimal scope):
- 6-week pilot, scope = web search reranking only (no store-edge for first run).
- Integration: simple SDK call or HTTP gateway; add a short proxy in front of their search service to capture signals (prefix caching helps).
- Success metrics: relative lift in CTR on search results (primary), conversion rate, 95th-pct latency under 250ms for web requests, incremental cost per conversion.
- Safety: keep existing ranking chain intact and run Redwood as a shadow/sidecar first (no live changes for first 2 weeks).

Technical fit notes (things to validate in discovery):
- Their current model size & token distribution. If <512 tokens and model family is transformer-based we can use medium quantized variant.
- Are they ok with a hosted endpoint hitting EU customers? If not, Private (VPC) or Dedicated in region required.
- Access patterns: mostly synchronous web requests; good candidate for batching + prefix cache.

Outbound sequence (first-pass):
1) Short cold email to Lena: subject = "Quick pilot idea to speed Moonscape search by 50ms+ and boost CTR". Body: 2 lines problem, 1 line pilot, 1 ask for 20-min intro + attach one-pager.
2) Follow-up to Marco (technical): 2–3 pain bullets + proposed integration sketch (proxy + SDK) + ask for a short tech sync.
3) If no response, ping via LinkedIn with a 1-sentence value tease and offer to demo a shadow test on sample dataset.

Sample email snippets (informal drafts):
- To Lena: "Lena — noticed Moonscape’s piece on scaling personalization. We ran a small pilot with a retailer that cut average rerank latency 37% and improved search CTR by 6 points using a shadow reranker + caching. Would you be open to a 20-min call to see if a similar pilot makes sense for Moonscape? I can share a short plan and an expected cost delta per 10k searches."
- To Marco: "Marco — hi, new to the team — quick tech sketch: put Redwood as a shadow reranker for 2 weeks, capture prefix cache stats, we’ll show per-request latency and cost delta. No changes to serving logic required. If helpful, we can run a synthetic load to validate P95 SLA against your baseline."

Objection handling (quick bullets):
- Objection: "We can’t send PII outside our VPC." Response: "We can run Private in your VPC or an on-prem package. Pilot can start as shadow with anonymized payloads to prove model impact first."
- Objection: "We can’t risk production uptime." Response: "Start shadow-only — no live changes. Rollout uses canary and automatic fallback to your baseline model if latency degrades."
- Objection: "We already have infra / this will add complexity." Response: "We provide an SDK + one small proxy pattern. For Dedicated customers we manage the capacity; for Private we provide deployable artifacts and a cutover checklist. We can also provide a 2-week runbook and run smoke tests with your SREs."
- Objection: "Cost unknown / unpredictable." Response: "Run a traffic-sampled simulation for an expected period. Optimize will generate concrete batching & caching suggestions and a predicted $/session. We’ll commit to a baseline reporting cadence during the pilot."

Discovery questions to ask in first 20-mins:
- What is the request volume for search reranks (per minute/hour)? Peak concurrency?
- Typical length of query + doc context you send to the reranker?
- Do you capture click signals / server logs we can use for offline evals?
- What are your security/compliance constraints (EU data, PCI scope, vendor whitelist)?
- Who owns the rollout decision and what timeline/budget windows are realistic?

Quick tactical notes / TO-DOs (me):
- Build one-pager (value props + pilot plan + expected metrics) — due EOD Tue.
- Prepare short demo: run offline rerank comparison on public dataset (simulate Moonscape) and capture latency & cost numbers — pair with Marco ask.
- Add contact intros to Outreach cadence and schedule LinkedIn touchpoints.
- Check if we have any existing customers in their vertical to get a quick 1-pager quote.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Need to validate whether their personalization stack already runs any on-prem transformers (if yes, messaging shifts to lowering ops burden).
- If Marco is new hire (joined Oct ’24) reach out with welcome note + technical sketch — high chance of an open conversation.
- Wonder if a quick benchmark (500 synthetic queries) hosted on Redwood Dedicated will be persuasive; estimate cost ~ $600 for the run (guesstimate).

Wrap: this is a high-relevance target (product pain + hiring signal). Keep outreach light + technical. Priority = get a 20-min sync with Marco and Lena; target opening week for demo/one-pager by next Tue.

Version notes: raw, iterative. Will convert to outbound sequence in Outreach once we have one-pager and offline evals.
